title: Computer Systems Engineers/Architects
description: Design and develop solutions to complex applications problems, system administration issues, or network concerns. Perform systems management and integration functions.

tasks.text: Communicate with staff or clients to understand specific system requirements.
Investigate system component suitability for specified purposes, and make recommendations regarding component use.
Provide customers or installation teams guidelines for implementing secure systems.
Direct the analysis, development, and operation of complete computer systems.
Direct the installation of operating systems, network or application software, or computer or network hardware.
Monitor system operation to detect potential problems.
Identify system data, hardware, or software components required to meet user needs.
Perform ongoing hardware and software maintenance operations, including installing or upgrading hardware or software.
Verify stability, interoperability, portability, security, or scalability of system architecture.
Research, test, or verify proper functioning of software patches and fixes.
Configure servers to meet functional specifications.
Collaborate with engineers or software developers to select appropriate design solutions or ensure the compatibility of system components.
Design and conduct hardware or software tests.
Evaluate existing systems to determine effectiveness, and suggest changes to meet organizational requirements.
Document design specifications, installation instructions, and other system-related information.
Perform security analyses of developed or packaged software components.
Provide technical guidance or support for the development or troubleshooting of systems.
Define and analyze objectives, scope, issues, or organizational impact of information systems.
Establish functional or system standards to address operational requirements, quality requirements, and design constraints.
Develop system engineering, software engineering, system integration, or distributed system architectures.
Provide advice on project costs, design concepts, or design changes.
Evaluate current or emerging technologies to consider factors such as cost, portability, compatibility, or usability.
Develop or approve project plans, schedules, or budgets.
Communicate project information through presentations, technical reports, or white papers.
Train system users in system operation or maintenance.
Complete models and simulations, using manual or automated tools, to analyze or predict system performance under different operating conditions.
Develop efficient and effective system controllers.
Develop application-specific software.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Adobe ActionScript, Adobe AIR, Aonix Software Through Pictures, Apache Ant.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Advanced business application programming ABAP, C#, C++, IBM ILOG.

skills.name: Application server software
skills.def: Software to support or run applications which provide services through a communication protocol. Examples: Atlassian Bitbucket, Docker, GitHub, GitLab.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud EC2, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Web Services AWS software, FileMaker Pro.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Apple macOS, Bash, Cisco IOS, Hewlett Packard HP-UX.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Adobe Flex, AJAX, Apache Groovy, Apache Struts.
